summary: A frozen Norwegian substitution key searched at the pinned budget; the 2%-noise control recovers but the clean search control fails, and the corpus is a modern 1930 Bible proxy.

method.selection: One manuscript search after the standard noisy control passed. No key adaptation after advisory or hidden results.

corpus_pins.title: Norwegian Bible (Bibelen på norsk, 1930), full Bible, one verse per line

limitations: The standard calibrate_cell power flag is search_cracks_control at 2% noise; it is true locally. The clean search flag is false. This nonmonotonic recovery is retained, not described as successful recovery of both controls.

The clean planted key passes all criteria except picture anchors, while the clean fitted key fails compression, reading and the not-illusion criterion. Fixed-budget search therefore does miss a known clean example; no claim of uniformly reliable recovery is made.
The reference is Norwegian riksmal/bokmal from a 1930 Bible, not a medieval Norwegian corpus. Any grid verdict is conditional on this corpus, family, view and budget.
Synthetic controls have no picture anchors. The calibration flag checks the project's specified non-anchor criteria and is not a full manuscript PASS.

continuation.reason: The desk returned lease gone before submission and its fresh brief contained only the ten standing mandates, with no concrete steps. The original lease was released without a PR. A new M-L3 mandate lease explicitly covers this completed language/cipher experiment.
continuation.local_advisory: The existing practice result is retained for the identical key. Source comparison from the search commit to the submission base shows no changes under vs/. Only the lease/step envelope and provenance change.
